en: A type of sweater or jumper that fastens up the front with buttons or a zipper, usually machine- or hand-knitted from wool.

cardigan.ety: Named after British military commander James Brudenell, 7th Earl of Cardigan (1797–1868). For the surname, see Cardigan.

ex.en: She put on a cardigan because it was cold.
ex.ja: 寒かったので彼女はカーディガンを着た。

note.ja: クリミア戦争の英国軍人カーディガン伯爵（Earl of Cardigan）の名前から。

zh: 行李傳送帶 /行李传送带

en: A pleasure ride, typically found at amusement parks and fairs and accompanied by music, consisting of a slowly revolving circular platfor…
A revolving device for item delivery or display.
To revolve or change places.

carousel.ety: From French carrousel, from Italian carosello, from Sicilian caruseḍḍu and/or Neapolitan carusiello. Uncertain. Some suggested a derivation from carro (“cart”), from Latin carrus, but this does not fit the criteria of an appropriate morphological reconstruction. Not believed to be related to carousal.

ex.en: The children are riding the carousel.
ex.ja: 子供たちはメリーゴーランドに乗ってるよ。

note.ja: フランス語 carrousel（騎馬試合）から。イタリア語 carosello。「回転木馬」→ 空港の回転台。

zh: 包皮環切術 /包皮环切术

en: The surgical excision of the foreskin and usually all or most of the penile frenulum.
Pharisaic circumcision.

ex.en: Circumcision is a religious custom in some cultures.
ex.ja: 割礼は一部の文化で行われる宗教的な慣習だ。

note.ja: circum（周りを）+ cis（切る）+ ion。周りを切ること →「割礼」。

en: Done or kept in secret, sometimes to conceal an illicit or improper purpose.
Not recognized as a regular member.

clandestine.ety: From Latin clandestīnus (“secret, concealed”); compare French clandestin.

ex.en: The two leaders held a clandestine meeting.
ex.ja: 二人の指導者は秘密の会談を行った。

note.ja: ラテン語 clandestinus（秘密の）から。clam（ひそかに）。「秘密の」。

en: A confused disordered jumble of things.
Background echoes, from clouds etc., on a radar or sonar screen.
To fill something with clutter.
To make a confused noise; to bustle.

clutter.ety: From Middle English cloteren (“to form clots; coagulate; heap on”), from clot (“clot”), equivalent to clot + -er (frequentative suffix). Compare Welsh cludair (“heap, pile”), cludeirio (“to heap”).

ex.en: Clear the clutter off your desk.
ex.ja: 机の上の散らかったものを片付けなさい。

note.ja: clot（固まり）の変化形とされる。「散らかり」。

en: The decayed remains of organic matter that has rotted into a natural fertilizer.
A medium in which one can cultivate plants.
To produce compost, let organic matter decay into fertilizer.

compost.ety: From Middle English compost, from Old Northern French compost (“a mixture of leaves, manure, etc., for fertilizing land, also a condiment”), from Latin compositus (“composed”), from componere. Doublet of compote, which was taken from modern French, composite, and kompot.

ex.en: We use kitchen waste to make compost.
ex.ja: 私たちは生ごみを使って堆肥を作っている。

note.ja: com（共に）+ pos（置く）+ t。一緒に置いて混ぜたもの →「堆肥」。compose（組み立てる）と同語源。

en: Someone who conquers.

conqueror.ety: From Middle English conquerour, from Old French conquereor, from conquerre. By surface analysis, conquer + -or.

ex.en: The conqueror ruled the land for decades.
ex.ja: 征服者は数十年にわたってその地を支配した。

note.ja: con（完全に）+ quer（得る）+ or。完全に手に入れる人 →「征服者」。

en: A simple bed, especially one for portable or temporary purposes.
A bed for infants or small children, with high, often slatted, often moveable sides.

cot.ety: Borrowed from Hindi खाट (khāṭ), from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀔𑀝𑁆𑀝𑀸 (khaṭṭā), from Sanskrit खट्वा (khaṭvā, “bedstead”).

ex.en: A baby is sleeping in the cot.
ex.ja: 赤ちゃんがベビーベッドで寝てるよ。

ex.en: Will you show me how to set up a cot?
ex.ja: 簡易ベッドの組み立て方を教えてもらえますか。

ex.en: I sleep on a cot.
ex.ja: 簡易ベッドで寝てるんだ。

note.ja: ヒンディー語 khāṭ（寝台）から。「簡易ベッド」。

en: Skillful at deceiving others.
Sneaky; surreptitious.

crafty.ety: From Middle English crafty, crefty, craftiȝ, from Old English cræftiġ (“ingenious; skilful; crafty; cunning; virtuous; powerful”), from Proto-West Germanic *kraftag, *kraftīg, *kraftug, from Proto-Germanic *kraftugaz (“powerful”), equivalent to craft + -y. Cognate with Saterland Frisian kräftich, krääftig, West Frisian krêftich, Dutch krachtig, German Low German krachtig, German kräftig.

ex.en: He is more crafty than wise.
ex.ja: 彼は賢いと言うよりはずるがしこい。

ex.en: The Germans are very crafty.
ex.ja: ドイツ人はとてもずる賢い。

note.ja: craft（技術・悪知恵）+ -y。「ずる賢い」。

en: The point at which something terminates or to which it is limited.
A cutoff point (cutoff value, threshold value, cutpoint): the amount set by an operational definition as the transition point between sta…
Constituting a limit or ending.
Designating a score or value demarcating the presence (or absence) of a disease, condition, or similar.

ex.en: The cutoff date for applications is May 1.
ex.ja: 申し込みの締め切りは５月１日だ。

note.ja: cut off（切り離す）の名詞化。「締め切り・遮断」。

en: An event or enterprise that ends suddenly and disastrously, often with humiliating consequences.
A breaking up of a natural dam, usually made of ice, by a river and the ensuing rush of water.

debacle.ety:
From French débâcle, from débâcler (“to unbar; unleash”) from prefix dé- (“un-”) + bâcler (“to dash, bind, bar, block”) [perhaps from unattested Middle French and Old French *bâcler, *bacler (“to hold in place, prop a door or window open”)], from Vulgar Latin *bacculare, from Latin baculum (“rod, staff used for support”), from Proto-Indo-European *bak-.
Also attested in Old French desbacler (“to clear a harbour by getting ships unloaded to make room for incoming ships with lading”) and in Occitan baclar (“to close”).
The hypothesised derivation from Middle Dutch *bakkelen (“to freeze artificia

ex.en: The opening ceremony was a complete debacle.
ex.ja: 開会式は大失敗だった。

note.ja: フランス語 débâcle（氷が割れて流れ出すこと）から。「崩壊・大失敗」。

en: Defying.
Boldly resisting opposition.
One who defies opposition.

defiant.ety: Borrowed from French défiant, from the verb défier. Doublet of diffident. By surface analysis, def(i) + -ant.

ex.en: He often takes a defiant attitude toward us.
ex.ja: 彼はしばしば挑戦的態度に出る。

ex.en: She was very surprised at his sudden defiant attitude.
ex.ja: 彼女は彼の突然の反抗的態度にとてもびっくりした。

ex.en: It is his defiant attitude that made the chief angry.
ex.ja: 彼の反抗的な態度に上司は腹を立てた。

note.ja: defy（逆らう）+ -ant。「反抗的な」。

en: Unusual of shape; misshapen.

ex.en: The tree was deformed by strong winds.
ex.ja: その木は強風で形がゆがんでいた。

note.ja: deform（変形させる）+ -ed。de + forma（形）。「変形した」。

en: To keep something from proceeding or coming to completion; to delay.
To keep someone from proceeding by holding them back or making claims on their attention.

detain.ety: From Old French detenir. Doublet of détente. Cognate with Italian detenere, Portuguese deter, Romanian deține, and Spanish detener.

ex.en: She is detaining the boy.
ex.ja: 彼女は男の子を引き止める。

ex.en: She detains the boy.
ex.ja: 彼女は男の子を引き止める。

note.ja: de（離れて）+ tain（保つ）。引き離して留めておく →「拘留する・引き留める」。detention（拘留）。

en: To deprive of weapons; to deprive of the means of attack or defense; to render defenseless.
To deprive of the means or the disposition to harm; to render harmless or innocuous.
The act of depriving a person of a weapon they carry.

disarm.ety: From Middle English desarmen (“to divest of arms”), from Anglo-Norman desarmer.

ex.en: The police managed to disarm the man.
ex.ja: 警察はなんとかその男の武器を取り上げた。

note.ja: dis（取り去る）+ arm（武装させる）。「武装解除する」→ 警戒を解かせる →「和ませる」。

en: A disadvantage; something that detracts or takes away.
A partial refund of an import fee, as when goods are re-exported from the country that collected the fee.

ex.en: Brilliant people have one major drawback - they don't know how to lose.
ex.ja: 優秀な人にはひとつ大きな欠点がある。負け方を知らないことだ。

ex.en: This system is bristling with defects and drawbacks.
ex.ja: この制度は欠陥だらけだ。

ex.en: His openness is a very positive quality, although not without its drawbacks.
ex.ja: 彼の寛容さは、難点が無いわけではないが、とても良い性向である。

note.ja: draw back（引き戻す）の名詞化。「足を引っ張るもの」→「欠点」。

en: In a shape of, or reminding of, an ellipse; oval.
Of, or showing ellipsis; having a word or words omitted.
An elliptical galaxy.
An elliptical trainer.

elliptical.ety: From elliptic + -al, from Ancient Greek ἐλλειπτικός (elleiptikós), from ἐλλείπω (elleípō, “I leave out, omit”).

ex.en: The orbit around Sirius is elliptical.
ex.ja: シリウスを回る軌道は楕円形である。

note.ja: ellipse（楕円）+ -ical。ギリシャ語 elleipsis（不足）。「省略的な」も同じ語源。

en: Fluently persuasive and articulate.
Effective in expressing meaning by speech.

ex.en: The eyes are as eloquent as the tongue.
ex.ja: 目は口ほどに物を言う。

ex.en: What an eloquent speaker he is!
ex.ja: 彼はまあなんて雄弁な話し手なんでしょう。

ex.en: The boy became more eloquent.
ex.ja: その少年は次第に雄弁になった。

note.ja: e（外へ）+ loqu（話す）+ ent。言葉が外へあふれ出る →「雄弁な」。

en: Someone of high rank, reputation or social status.
The quality or state of being eminent.

eminence.ety: From Old French eminence, from Latin ēminentia (“prominence”, “protuberance”; “eminence”, “excellence”).

ex.en: She figured as a gray eminence.
ex.ja: 彼女は黒幕としてかかわっていた。

ex.en: He won eminence as a scientist.
ex.ja: 彼は科学者として名声をあげた。

note.ja: eminent（著名な）+ -ence。ラテン語 eminere（突き出る）。「著名・高所」。

en: Of, near, or relating to the equator.
Relating to the midline of any approximately spherical object.
A kind of telescope mounted so as to have two axes of motion at right angles to each other, one of them parallel to the axis of the Earth…

ex.en: Equatorial countries are hot all year.
ex.ja: 赤道付近の国は一年中暑い。

note.ja: equator（赤道）+ -ial。「赤道の」。

en: The ball of the eye.
An instance of eyeballing something.
To gauge, estimate or judge by eye, rather than measuring precisely; to look or glance at.
To stare at intently.

eyeball.ety: From eye + ball. Compare Middle English balle off the eye, balle of þe eyȝe (“eyeball”, literally “ball of the eye”).

ex.en: Is it safe to eat a pig's eyeball?
ex.ja: 豚の眼球は食べても大丈夫なんですか？

note.ja: eye + ball（球）。「眼球」。

en: Deceptive or false appearance; that which misleads the eye or the mind.
An argument, or apparent argument, which professes to be decisive of the matter at issue, while in reality it is not; a specious argument.

fallacy.ety: From Middle English fallaci, fallace, fallas, from Old French fallace (whence -acy), from Latin fallācia (“deception, deceit”), from fallāx (“deceptive, deceitful”), from fallere (“to deceive”).

ex.en: It is a fallacy that money brings happiness.
ex.ja: お金が幸せをもたらすというのは誤った考えだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 fallacia（欺き）から。fallere（だます）。「誤った考え」。false と同じ。

en: Deficient in physical strength.
Lacking force, vigor, or effectiveness in action or expression; faint.

feeble.ety:
Etymology tree
Anglo-Norman feblebor.
Middle English feble
English feeble
From Middle English feble, from Anglo-Norman feble (“weak, feeble”) (compare French faible), from Latin flēbilis (“tearful, mournful, lamentable”) by dissimilation, from fleō (“to weep, cry”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰleh₁-. Doublet of foible.

ex.en: The feeble patient is suffering from stomach cancer.
ex.ja: その弱々しい患者は胃癌に苦しんでいる。

ex.en: The old lady has been rather feeble since her illness.
ex.ja: その老婦人は病後かなり体力が弱っている。

ex.en: He was too feeble to do manual labor.
ex.ja: 彼は非常に身体が弱くて力仕事はできなかった。

note.ja: ラテン語 flebilis（泣くべき・哀れな）から。flere（泣く）。「弱々しい」。

en: Marked by extreme and violent energy.
Extreme or intense.

ferocious.ety: Taken from Latin ferōx (“wild, bold, savage, fierce”) + -ous.

ex.en: A ferocious storm hit the coast.
ex.ja: 猛烈な嵐が海岸を襲った。

note.ja: ラテン語 ferox（猛々しい）から。ferus（野生の）。「凶暴な」。fierce と同じ。

en: The study of formal debate; rhetoric.
A type of rhetoric or debate society or club, particularly one affiliated with a school.

ex.ja: 科学捜査の専門家が犯行現場を調べた。

note.ja: forensic（法廷の）+ -s。ラテン語 forum（広場・法廷）。forum と同じ。

en: Sweet-smelling; having a pleasant (usually strong) scent or fragrance.
Attractive.

fragrant.ety: Borrowed from Latin frāgrāns, present active participle of frāgrō (“to smell”).

ex.en: These flowers are not only beautiful but also fragrant.
ex.ja: この花は美しいだけでなく、よい香りがします。

ex.en: The garden is fragrant with the smell of roses.
ex.ja: 庭には薔薇の花が香っている。

ex.en: She planted fragrant olives in the garden.
ex.ja: 彼女は庭に木犀を植えた。

note.ja: ラテン語 fragrare（香る）の現在分詞。「香りのよい」。fragrance と同じ。

en: Brave, valiant, courteous, especially with regard to male attitudes towards women.
Honorable.
One who woos, a lover, a suitor, a seducer.
A topgallant.
To conduct, escort, convey.
To behave in a gallant fashion; to act the gallant.

gallant.ety: From Middle English galant, galaunt, from Old French galant (“courteous; dashing; brave”), present participle of galer (“to rejoice; make merry”), from gale (“pomp; show; festivity; mirth”); either from Frankish *wala (“good, well”), a variant form of *wela, from Proto-Germanic *wela (whence well), from Proto-Indo-European *welh₁- (“to choose, wish”); or alternatively from Frankish *gail (“merry; mirthful; proud; luxuriant”), from Proto-Germanic *gailaz (“merry; excited; luxurious”), related to Dutch geil (“horny; lascivious; salacious; lecherous”), German geil (“randy; horny; lecherous; wicke

ex.en: All the soldiers were gallant.
ex.ja: 兵士は皆勇敢だった。

note.ja: 古フランス語 galer（楽しむ）の現在分詞。「華やかな」→「勇敢な・（女性に）親切な」。gala と同じ。

The formulation of general concepts from specific instances by abstracting common properties.

en: A person who makes, repairs or sells things of gold, especially jewelry.

goldsmith.ety: From Middle English goldsmith, from Old English goldsmiþ (“goldsmith”), from Proto-Germanic *gulþasmiþaz (“goldsmith”), equivalent to gold + smith. Cognate with Scots goldsmyth, gouldsmeth (“goldsmith”), Saterland Frisian Gouldsmid (“goldsmith”), West Frisian goudsmid (“goldsmith”), Dutch goudsmid (“goldsmith”), German Goldschmied (“goldsmith”), Danish guldsmed (“goldsmith”), Swedish guldsmed (“goldsmith”), Icelandic gullsmiður (“goldsmith”). Eclipsed non-native Middle English orbatour, orbatur (“goldsmith”) and orfever, orfevre (“goldsmith”), both borrowed from Old French.

ex.en: The goldsmith made a beautiful ring.
ex.ja: 金細工師が美しい指輪を作った。

note.ja: gold（金）+ smith（職人）。「金細工師」。blacksmith と対。

en: A fastening consisting of two metal rings, designed to go around a person's wrists, and connected by a chain or hinge.
Any abstract constraint, such as rules, regulations, or lack of resources.

handcuffs.ety:
1775, from hand + cuff (“end of shirtsleeve”).
Possibly influenced by Old English handcops, from hand + cops (“fetter, chains”), but due to lack of continuity (centuries between Old English and modern term), generally analyzed as a re-invention.

ex.en: I put handcuffs on him.
ex.ja: 私は彼に手錠をかけた。

note.ja: hand（手）+ cuffs（袖口）。「手錠」。

en: A religious recluse; someone who lives alone for religious reasons; an eremite.
A recluse; someone who lives alone and shuns human companionship.

hermit.ety: From Middle English hermite, heremite, eremite, from Old French eremite, from Ecclesiastical Latin, Late Latin eremita, from Ancient Greek ἐρημίτης (erēmítēs, “person of the desert”) from ἐρημία (erēmía, “desert, solitude”), from ἔρημος (érēmos) or ἐρῆμος (erêmos, “uninhabited”) plus -ίτης (-ítēs, “one connected to, a member of”). Doublet of eremite. Displaced native Old English ānsetla.

ex.en: The hermit lived in a wooden hut.
ex.ja: 隠者は木造の小屋に住んでいた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 erēmitēs（荒野に住む人）から。erēmos（さびしい・荒野）。「世捨て人」。hermit crab（ヤドカリ）。

en: To make difficult to accomplish; to act as an obstacle; to frustrate.
To delay or impede; to keep back, to prevent.
Of or belonging to that part or end which is in the rear or hind, or which follows.

hinder.ety: From Middle English hindren, from Old English hindrian, from Proto-Germanic *hindrōną, *hinderōną (“to hinder”), from Proto-Germanic *hinder (“back”) (adverb). Cognate with Dutch hinderen and German hindern, Latin contra (“back, against”).

ex.en: He didn't come to help, but to hinder us.
ex.ja: 彼は助けに来たというより邪魔しに来た。

ex.en: She didn't come to help, but to hinder us.
ex.ja: 彼女は我々の手伝いに来たというより、邪魔しに来たようなものだ。

ex.en: Don't hinder me in my work.
ex.ja: 私の仕事を邪魔しないでくれ。

note.ja: 古英語 hindrian（妨げる）から。behind と同系。「後ろへ引き止める」→「妨げる」。

A soldier on horseback, especially a cavalryman.

Owing gratitude for a service or favour.

ex.ja: 僕は彼に少なからず恩義がある。

en: Offensive to good taste.
Not in keeping with conventional moral values; improper, immodest, or unseemly.

ex.en: He has given us indecent wages.
ex.ja: 彼はわたしらに少ない賃金しかくれなかった。

ex.en: He reformed his indecent ways.
ex.ja: 彼は淫らな生活から足を洗った。

note.ja: in（否定）+ decent（きちんとした）。「下品な」。

en: A formal investigation, often held before a jury, especially one into the cause of a death
An inquiry, typically into an undesired outcome

inquest.ety: From Middle English enquest, from Old French enqueste (Modern French enquête), from Vulgar Latin inquirere, or from Medieval Latin inquesta < in + Latin quaesita.

ex.ja: その男性の死について検死審問が開かれた。

note.ja: ラテン語 inquisita（調べられたもの）から。in + quaerere（求める）。「検死・審問」。inquire と同じ。

To make a noise of metal or glass clattering against itself.
To cause to make a noise of metal or glass clattering against itself.

To gasp for breath as in a severe fit of coughing.
A tight curl, twist, or bend in a length of rope, line, or other long cylindrical material, such as hair etc.

ex.ja: 庭のホースがよじれている。

To transport by, or as if by, lorry.

lorry.ety: Uncertain; perhaps from dialectal English lurry (“to lug or pull about, drag”) (compare dialectal lurry-cart), or from the forename Laurie. First attested in early to middle 19th century.

ex.ja: もう少しでトラックにはねられるところだった。

ex.ja: イギリスではトラックはローリーと呼ばれる。

ex.ja: 積み荷が落ちたので、トラックは停車しなければならなかった。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。lurry（引く）とされる。（英）「トラック」。

en: A tree or shrub in any species of the genus Magnolia, many with large flowers and simple leaves.
The flower of a magnolia tree.
Of a creamy white colour, like that of some magnolia flowers.

.

ex.ja: モクレンの木が早春に花を咲かせた。

ex.ja: 色がうまく調合しない。

ex.ja: 彼は恐怖と驚きの混ざった表情をしていた。

A set of names or terms.

ex.ja: 科学者たちは植物に標準的な命名法を使っている。

ex.ja: 彼らはオーストラリアの奥地を車で横断した。

ex.ja: 普通の人間は天使の叫びが聞こえない。

note.ja: philanthropy（慈善）+ -ic。「慈善の」。

ex.ja: 子どもたちは庭に遊び小屋を作った。

note.ja: play（劇）+ house。「劇場」。

ex.ja: 私はアメリカ滞在の期間を延長したい。

ex.en: Gooseberries can prolong your life.
ex.ja: スグリは長寿に有効な果物だ。

note.ja: pro（前へ）+ longus（長い）。「長引かせる」。prolonged と同じ。

ex.ja: プロパンはガスだよ。

A gentle hike.

ex.ja: サラは祖父母が昔話をくどくどとしゃべるのを聞くとうんざりする。

To instruct to go, inquire, elsewhere.
A redirection.
An examination of a witness, following cross-examination, by the party that conducted the direct examination, re-examination.

ex.ja: そのウェブサイトは新しいページへ自動的に移動します。

ex.ja: 雨が一日中絶え間なく降っていた。

ex.ja: 熱帯の太陽は容赦なくぎらぎら照り付けた。

en: A potentiometer with a linearly sliding control.

The meaning "small hamburger" was originally used to describe onion-steamed small burgers at White Castle restaurants, formerly spelt "Slyder".

ex.en: Move the slider to adjust the volume.
ex.ja: つまみを動かして音量を調節してください。

note.ja: slide（滑る）+ -er。「スライダー」。

en: Astonished; taken aback.

ex.ja: 市民達は激しい爆撃を受けてひるんだ。

note.ja: stagger（よろめかせる・ずらす）+ -ed。「時差の・ずらした」→「驚いた」。

ex.ja: 毎年１ヶ月の休暇をもらうことが契約の条項になっている。

note.ja: stipulate（規定する）+ -ed。ラテン語 stipulari（約束させる）。「規定された」。

One who subverts, a saboteur, provocateur, or propagandist.

The subset of those names other than the one to be used according to the rules.

ex.ja: 「small」と「little」は同義語です。

ex.ja: 「small」と「little」は同義語です。

Something that is done or produced habitually or characteristically.
To exhibit a tic; to undergo a sudden, semi-voluntary muscle movement.

en: One in a series of volumes.

ex.ja: 彼は歴史についての分厚い本を持ち歩いていた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 tomos（切り取られたもの・巻）から。「大冊」。atom、epitome と同じ tom。

note.ja: total（全体の）+ -itarian。イタリアのファシズム期の語。「全体主義の」。

en: The act of walking with heavy steps.
Any ship which does not have a fixed schedule or published ports of call.
To walk with heavy footsteps.
To walk for a long time (usually through difficult terrain).

tramp.ety:
From Middle English trampen (“to walk heavily”), from Middle Low German trampen (“to stamp”) (trampeln (“to walk with heavy steps”), see trample) or from Middle Dutch trampen (“to stamp”), from Proto-West Germanic *trampan (“to step”). Doublet of tremp.
Cognate with Dutch trampen (“to stamp, kick, step”), dialectal German trampen (“to step, walk, tread”), whence commoner German trampeln (“to trample”). Probably related to trap.

ex.en: I can't bear to tramp ten miles in this heat.
ex.ja: この暑さに１０マイルもてくてく歩くのはたまらない。

ex.ja: 泥だらけの足で居間をどたどたあるいてはいけない。

ex.ja: 野犬がうちの庭を踏み荒した。

note.ja: 中英語 trampen（踏みつける）から。「どしどし歩く」→ 歩き回る人 →「浮浪者」。trample と同じ。

The edible head or curd of a cauliflower plant.
To (cause to) swell up like a cauliflower ear.

cauliflower.ety: From 16th century cole-florye, equivalent to cole (from Latin caulis) + flower, reformed to more closely match the Latin etymon. By surface analysis, caul(is) + -i- + flower. Cognate with French chou-fleur, Italian cavolfiore.

ex.en: I like broccoli, but I hate cauliflower.
ex.ja: ブロッコリーは好きですが、カリフラワーは大嫌いです。

ex.en: Cauliflower and broccoli are similar.
ex.ja: カリフラワーとブロッコリーは似てます。

note.ja: イタリア語 cavolfiore ＝ cavolo（キャベツ）+ fiore（花）。「花キャベツ」。kale と同じ。

en: A power saw that has a power-driven and fast-revolving chain of metal teeth, usually used to cut trees.
To cut with a chainsaw.
To make quick and substantial spending cuts.

chainsaw.ety: Compound of chain + saw in reference to the chain-cutting mechanism.

ex.en: Why do you need a chainsaw?
ex.ja: なんでチェーンソーが必要なの？

note.ja: chain（鎖）+ saw（のこぎり）。「チェーンソー」。

en: A distinctive member (Acinonyx jubatus) of the cat family, slightly smaller than the leopard, but with proportionately longer limbs and a…

cheetah.ety: Borrowed from Hindi चीता (cītā, “leopard, panther”), ultimately from Sanskrit चित्र (citra, “multicolored, speckled”) (akin to Old High German haitar (“bright”) > German heiter; Old Norse heiðr (“bright”)) + Sanskrit काय (kāya, “body”), thus “having a spotted body”.

ex.en: A cheetah runs as fast as any animal.
ex.ja: チータは他のどの動物にも劣らず速く走る。

ex.en: The cheetah is the fastest animal.
ex.ja: 一番速い動物はチーターです。

ex.en: Cheetahs cannot climb trees.
ex.ja: チーターは木には登れないんだ。

note.ja: ヒンディー語 cītā（まだらの）から。サンスクリット語 citra（まだらの）。

en: Of, relating to, or influenced by climate.

climatic.ety:
Etymology tree
English climate
Proto-Indo-European *-ikos
Proto-Italic *-ikos
Latin -icuslbor.
Old French -iquebor.
Middle English -ik
English -ic
English climatic
From climate + -ic.

ex.en: Global climatic changes may have been responsible for the extinction of the dinosaurs.
ex.ja: 地球的規模の気候の変化が原因で恐竜が絶滅したのかもしれない。

note.ja: climate + -ic。「気候の」。climactic（最高潮の）と区別。

en: In a curve or twist corresponding to the movement of the hands of a clock.
Moving clockwise; having rotary motion in the manner of a clock.

clockwise.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Celtic *klokkosder.?
Early Medieval Latin cloccader.
Old Northern French cloquebor.
Old Dutch *klokka
Middle Dutch clockebor.
Middle English clokke
English clock

Middle English -wis
English -wise
English clockwise
From clock + -wise.

ex.en: The top part is turning clockwise.
ex.ja: 上部は時計回りに回ってます。

ex.en: Turn the knob clockwise.
ex.ja: ノブを時計回りに回して。

ex.en: Normal screws when turned clockwise will tighten and when turned anti-clockwise will loosen.
ex.ja: 普通ネジはね、のの字に回すと締まって、のの字の反対に回すと緩むんだよ。

note.ja: clock（時計）+ -wise（〜の方向に）。「時計回りに」。otherwise と同じ -wise。

ja: ぜんまい仕掛け（like clockwork：規則正しく）

en: A mechanism powered by a coiled spring and regulated by some form of escapement; the power is transmitted through toothed gearwheels and …
The action of behaving mechanically in the manner of a clock.
Driven by clockwork.
Very smooth and regular.

clockwork.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Celtic *klokkosder.?
Early Medieval Latin cloccader.
Old Northern French cloquebor.
Old Dutch *klokka
Middle Dutch clockebor.
Middle English clokke
English clock
English -work
English clockwork
From clock + -work.

ex.en: The public transportation system runs like clockwork.
ex.ja: 公共の交通輸送機関は正確に動いています。

ex.en: He devised a complicated clockwork toy.
ex.ja: 彼は複雑なぜんまいじかけのおもちゃを考案した。

note.ja: clock + work（仕掛け）。「ぜんまい仕掛け」→「規則正しく（like clockwork）」。

en: The state of things being similar or identical.
A point of resemblance; a similarity.

conformity.ety: From Middle English conformyte, from Middle French conformité. By surface analysis, conform + -ity.

ex.en: Conformity is an essential element of our homogeneous community.
ex.ja: 同じような人々からなる私たちの地域社会では、体裁に従おうとする意識は不可欠な要素である。

note.ja: con（共に）+ form（形）+ ity。形を同じにすること →「順応・一致」。conform（従う）。

en: The spouse of a monarch.
A husband, wife, companion or partner.
of a title, by virtue of one's (living) spouse; often contrasted with regnant and dowager
To associate or keep company (with).
To be in agreement.

consort.ety: Borrowed from Middle French, ultimately from Latin cōnsors. As “companion or partner”, via Middle English consorte.

ex.en: The queen's consort attended the ceremony.
ex.ja: 女王の配偶者が式典に出席した。

note.ja: ラテン語 consors（運命を共にする人）から。con + sors（運命）。「配偶者・交際する」。consortium と同じ。

en: To compare things and bring them into a relation having corresponding characteristics.
To be related by a correlation; to be correlated.
Either of a pair of things related by a correlation; a correlative.

ex.en: Test scores often correlate with sleep.
ex.ja: テストの点数はしばしば睡眠と相関する。

note.ja: cor（共に）+ relate。「相関する」。

en: Showing regard or thought for others; especially, displaying good manners or etiquette.

courteous.ety:
From Middle English curteis, from Old French curteis (French courtois), from cort (“court”). By surface analysis, court + -eous.
Compare typologically Czech zdvořilý (<~ dvůr), German höflich (<~ Hof). Also note Russian прийти́сь ко двору́ (prijtísʹ ko dvorú).
Compare typologically civil, urbane. See pagan for the opposite.

ex.en: You must be courteous to any guest.
ex.ja: あなたはどんなお客にも礼儀を尽くさねばならない。

ex.en: It is very courteous of you to call on me.
ex.ja: 訪ねてきてくださって本当にありがとうございます。

ex.en: It was courteous of him to write a letter of thanks.
ex.ja: 礼状を書くとは彼も礼儀正しかった。

note.ja: courtesy（礼儀）と同じ。古フランス語 corteis（宮廷風の）。court（宮廷）+ -eous。「礼儀正しい」。

en: In a curious manner; with curiosity; inquisitively.
Oddly; in a strange or unexpected way.

curiously.ety: From Middle English curiusly, curyously, curiosly, curiouseliche, curyouslyche, equivalent to curious + -ly.

ex.en: The townspeople looked curiously at me.
ex.ja: 町の人達は物珍しそうに私を見た。

ex.en: Curiously, a flower bloomed on the withered up tree.
ex.ja: 奇妙なことに枯れた木に花が咲いた。

note.ja: curious（好奇心の強い・奇妙な）+ -ly。「物珍しそうに・奇妙なことに」。

en: To delay or postpone.
to postpone induction into military service.

defer.ety: Originally a variant of (and hence a doublet of) differ; from Middle English differren (“to postpone”), from Old French differer, from Latin differō. Doublet of differ and dilate. See also infer, collate and confer, delate and defer, relate and refer as well as prelate and prefer among others.

ex.en: I defer to your judgement.
ex.ja: 私は君の判断を尊重する。

note.ja: ラテン語 differre（先へ運ぶ）から。「延期する」→ 判断を相手に任せる →「従う（defer to）」。differ と同じ語源。

en: The process of destroying a forest and replacing it with something else, especially with an agricultural system.
A transformation to eliminate intermediate data structures within a program.

deforestation.ety:

Proto-Indo-European *déh₁

From deforest + -ation. First attested in 1870.

ex.en: Their habitat is threatened by deforestation.
ex.ja: 彼らの生息地は、森林破壊に脅かされています。

note.ja: de（取り去る）+ forest + -ation。「森林破壊」。

en: The social, non-verbal behaviors (such as body language and facial expressions) that are characteristic of a person.

demeanor.ety: From Middle English demenure, from the verb Middle English demenen, demeinen (“to handle, manage”), from Old French demener (“to guide, conduct”), from de- + mener (“to conduct, lead”), from Latin *mināre (“to drive”) and minor (“to project or jut forth”).

ex.en: The teacher had a cold demeanor.
ex.ja: 先生は冷ややかだった。

ex.en: She has a graceful demeanor.
ex.ja: 彼女の物腰はしとやかだ。

note.ja: demean（ふるまう）+ -or。古フランス語 demener（導く）。「態度・物腰」。

en: To be felt sorrow for; worthy of compassion; lamentable.
Deserving strong condemnation; shockingly bad, wretched.
A person or thing that is to be deplored.

deplorable.ety:
The adjective is borrowed from French déplorable (“lamentable, regrettable”), or from its etymon Late Latin dēplōrābilis + English -able (suffix meaning ‘relevant to, suitable to’). Dēplōrābilis is derived from Latin dēplōrō (“to bemoan, complain about; to bewail, lament, deplore”) + -ābilis (suffix meaning ‘able or worthy to be’); while dēplōrō is from dē- (intensifying prefix) + plōrō (“to cry out; to complain; to lament, deplore”) (possibly from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₃(w)- (“to flow; to swim”)). By surface analysis, deplore + -able.
The noun is derived from the adjective. Noun sense 2 re

ex.en: It is deplorable that she is so selfish.
ex.ja: 彼女がこれほど自分勝手なのは嘆かわしい。

note.ja: deplore（嘆く）+ -able。de + plorare（泣く）。「嘆かわしい」。explore と同じ plor。

en: Disturbed or upset, especially mentally.
Insane.

ex.en: He became temporarily deranged.
ex.ja: 彼は一時的に精神が錯乱状態になった。

note.ja: derange（狂わせる）+ -ed。de + range（並べる）。「列を乱す」→「狂わせる」。

en: Any non-soap cleaning agent, especially a synthetic surfactant.
Synonym of cleansing.

detergent.ety: From French détergent, from Latin dētergēns, the present participle of dētergeō, from dē (“off”) + tergeō (“wipe, polish”).

ex.en: I like this detergent because it lathers well.
ex.ja: この洗剤、泡立ちがいいから気に入ってる。

ex.en: Are there any detergents in the laundry?
ex.ja: ランドリーには洗剤がありますか。

ex.en: Did you change detergents?
ex.ja: 洗剤かえた？

note.ja: ラテン語 detergere（ぬぐい去る）から。de + tergere（ふく）。「洗剤」。

en: A diversion or deviation from one's original route.
A temporary alternative route available to motorists away from the usual route due to a closure for repairs, dealing with an accident, or…
To make a detour.
To direct or send on a detour.

detour.ety: Borrowed from French détour, from détourner (“turn away”).

ex.en: I think I will take a detour to return home.
ex.ja: 今日は遠回りをして帰ろっと。

ex.en: We had to make a detour across a bridge down the river from here.
ex.ja: 私たちは川下にある橋を渡って回り道をしなければならなかった。

note.ja: フランス語 détour（回り道）から。dé + tourner（回る）。「回り道」。turn と同じ。

en: Time lost due to the failure of some system or machinery, such as a computer crash or power outage.
A period of time when work or other activity is less intense or stops.

downtime.ety: From down (“out of order; out of service; inoperable”) + time.

ex.en: The website had two hours of downtime last night.
ex.ja: そのウェブサイトは昨夜２時間停止していた。

note.ja: down（停止）+ time。「休止時間」。

en: Towards a lower place; towards what is below.
Towards something which is lower in order, smaller, inferior, etc.
Downward.

downwards.ety:
Etymology tree
Old English of-

Old English dūne
Old English ofdūne
Old English adūne
Old English dūne
Middle English doun
English down
English -wards
English downwards
From down + -wards.

ex.en: The road slopes downwards to the sea.
ex.ja: 道は海に向かって下り坂になっている。

note.ja: down + -wards。「下の方へ」。

en: An act or instance of making something larger.
A making more obvious or serious; exacerbation.

enlargement.ety:
Etymology tree
English enlarge

From enlarge + -ment.

ex.en: I ordered an enlargement of this photo.
ex.ja: この写真の引き伸ばしを注文した。

note.ja: enlarge（拡大する）+ -ment。「拡大」。

en: To consider or assert as equal or equivalent (to or with).
To make equal or equivalent.
A statement in assembly language that defines a symbol having a particular value.

equate.ety: From Middle English equaten, from Latin aequātus, perfect passive participle of aequō, see -ate (verb-forming suffix).

ex.en: Freedom is usually equated with doing whatever you like.
ex.ja: 自由とはたいてい、やりたいことを何でもやることと同一視される。

ex.en: They equate religion with church-going.
ex.ja: 彼らは宗教イコール教会に行くことだと考えている。

ex.en: It is foolish to equate money with happiness.
ex.ja: 金を幸福と同一視するなんてばかげたことだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 aequare（等しくする）から。aequus。「同一視する」。equal、equation と同じ。

en: Of horseback riding or horseback riders.
Of or relating to the ancient Roman class of equites.
One who rides a horse.
Synonym of eques.

equestrian.ety: Ultimately from Latin equester (“of or pertaining to equestrians/cavalry”) + -ianus (“-ian, related to”, adjective marker), from equus (“horse”).

ex.en: Equestrian is the only mixed-gender Olympic event.
ex.ja: 馬術競技は男女混合で行われる唯一のオリンピック競技です。

note.ja: ラテン語 equester（騎手の）から。equus（馬）。

ja: この世のものとも思えない

en: Pertaining to the presupposition of an invisible air-like element permeating all of space, or to the higher regions beyond the earth or b…
Pertaining to the immaterial realm, as symbolically represented by, or (in earlier epochs) conflated with, such atmospheric and extra-atm…

ethereal.ety: From Latin aetherius (“of or pertaining to the ether, the sky, Heaven or the air or upper air”), from Ancient Greek αἰθέριος (aithérios, “of or pertaining to the upper air”). By surface analysis, ether + -ial.

ex.en: The singer has an ethereal voice.
ex.ja: その歌手はこの世のものとは思えない声をしている。

note.ja: ether（天空の上層）+ -eal。ギリシャ語 aithēr（澄んだ上空の空気）。「この世のものとも思えない」。

en: A wide stretch, usually of sea, sky, or land.
An amount of spread or stretch.

ex.en: We looked out over the vast expanse of the desert.
ex.ja: 私たちは広大な砂漠を見渡した。

note.ja: ラテン語 expansum（広げられたもの）から。「広がり」。expand と同じ。

en: A flourish of trumpets or horns as to announce; a short and lively air performed on hunting horns during the chase.
A show of ceremony or celebration.
To play a fanfare.
To embellish with fanfares.

fanfare.ety: Borrowed from French fanfare; some senses apparently influenced by surface analysis, fan + fare.

ex.en: The new product was launched with great fanfare.
ex.ja: その新製品は鳴り物入りで発売された。

note.ja: フランス語 fanfare から。擬音的な語とされる。「ファンファーレ」→「鳴り物入りの宣伝」。

en: In a favorable manner.

favorably.ety:

From favorable + -ly.

ex.en: Every successful repetition spoke favorably for the quality of the first test.
ex.ja: うまく行われれば何回実験を繰り返しても、最初の実験の質が十分保証されるのだった。

ex.en: The applicant impressed the examiner favorably.
ex.ja: その志望者は試験官に好ましい印象を与えた。

note.ja: favorable + -ly。「好意的に・有利に」。

en: The hard, flat translucent covering near the tip of a human finger, useful for scratching and fine manipulation.

fingernail.ety: From Middle English finger neil(e); equivalent to finger + nail. Compare Middle English nayl of fynger (“fingernail”) and Old English handnæġl (“fingernail”). Compare also Saterland Frisian Fingernail (“fingernail”), West Frisian fingerneil (“fingernail”), Dutch vingernagel (“fingernail”), German Fingernagel (“fingernail”), Danish fingernegl (“fingernail”), Swedish fingernagel (“fingernail”), Norwegian fingernegl (“fingernail”), Icelandic fingurnögl (“fingernail”).

ex.en: I broke my fingernail.
ex.ja: 爪が割れちゃった。

ex.en: I can't find my fingernail clippers.
ex.ja: 爪切りが見当たらないんだよ。

ex.en: One of Tom's bad habits is biting his fingernails.
ex.ja: トムの悪い癖の１つは、爪を噛むことだね。

note.ja: finger（指）+ nail（爪）。「指の爪」。

en: Someone (especially male) who is skilled in the work of fighting fire.
A person (originally a man) who keeps the fire going underneath a steam boiler (originally, shoveling coal by hand), particularly on a ra…

fireman.ety:

From fire + -man.

ex.ja: 消防士たちはすぐに火を消した。

ex.en: The firemen had the fire out in no time.
ex.ja: 消防士はあっという間に火を消した。

ex.en: The fireman soon put the fire out.
ex.ja: 消防士はまもなく火事を消した。

note.ja: fire + man。「消防士」。性別を問わない言い方は firefighter。

en: A narrow-necked vessel of metal or glass, used for various purposes; as of sheet metal, to carry gunpowder in; or of wrought iron, to con…
A container used to discreetly carry a small amount of a hard alcoholic beverage; a pocket flask.
To invest a denture in a flask so as to produce a sectional mold.

flask.ety:
From Middle English flask, flaske (“case, cask, keg”), from Old English flasce, flaxe (“bottle, flask”) and Medieval Latin flascō (“bottle”); from Frankish *flaskā; both from Proto-Germanic *flaskǭ (“braid-covered bottle, wicker-enclosed jug”), from Proto-Indo-European *ploḱ-skō (“flat”), or from Proto-Indo-European *pleḱ- (“to weave”). Doublet of fiasco, flacon, and flagon.
Related to Dutch fles; also German Low German Flaske, Fless, German Flasche, Danish flaske; also Lithuanian plókščias, Czech ploský, Albanian flashkët.
The sense “laboratory glassware” is from Italian fiasco, and the sense

ex.en: He carried a flask of hot tea.
ex.ja: 彼は熱いお茶の入った水筒を持っていた。

note.ja: 中世ラテン語 flasca（瓶）から。「フラスコ・水筒」。fiasco と同じ語源。

en: Anything light, soft or fuzzy, especially fur, hair, feathers.
Anything inconsequential or superficial.
To make something fluffy.
To become fluffy, puff up.

fluff.ety:
From earlier floow (“woolly substance, down, nap, lint”), also spelt flough, flue, and flew, from West Flemish vluwe,
of uncertain ultimate origin:
* Compare Old English flōh (“that which is flown off, fragment, piece”); see flaw
* Possibly representing a blend of flue + puff; compare Middle Dutch vloe, or perhaps onomatopoeic; compare dialectal English floose, flooze, fleeze (“particles of wool or cotton; fluff; loose threads or fibres”), Danish fnug (“down, fluff”), Swedish fnugg (“speck, flake”).
* Alternatively, West Flemish vluwe may derive from French velu (“hairy, furry”), from Latin vi

ex.en: There's some fluff on your sweater.
ex.ja: セーターに綿ぼこりが付いているよ。

note.ja: 擬態的な語。「綿毛」→ 中身のない「くだらないもの」。

en: In a fond manner; affectionately; tenderly.

fondly.ety: From Middle English fondly, fondely, fonnedli, equivalent to fond + -ly.

ex.en: My mother gazed at me fondly.
ex.ja: 母は優しい目で私を見た。

note.ja: fond + -ly。「愛情をこめて・懐かしく」。

zh: 腳註 /脚注 or 腳注 /脚注

en: A short piece of text, often numbered, placed at the bottom of a printed page, that adds a comment, citation, reference etc, to a designa…
An event of lesser importance than some larger event to which it is related.
To add footnotes to a text.

ex.en: The footnotes are at the bottom of the page.
ex.ja: 脚注はページの下欄にある。

ex.en: Footnotes are notes at the foot of a page.
ex.ja: 脚注とはページの下部の注をいう。

ex.en: See the footnote on page 5.
ex.ja: ５ページ脚注を参照してください。

note.ja: foot（下部）+ note（注）。「ページの下の注」→「脚注」。

en: Cold, chilly; icy.
Having frost on it or in it.

frosty.ety:
From Middle English frosty, forsty, from Old English forstiġ, fyrstiġ (“frosty”), from Proto-West Germanic *frostag, *frustīg, By surface analysis, frost + -y.
Cognates
Cognate with West Frisian froastich (“frosty”), Dutch vorstig (“frosty”), German Low German fröstig (“frosty”), German frostig (“frosty”), Swedish frostig (“frosty”). Compare also Saterland Frisian froasterch (“frosty”), German Low German frösterg (“frosty”).

ex.en: It was a frosty morning.
ex.ja: 霜の降りた朝だった。

note.ja: frost（霜）+ -y。「霜の降りた」→「冷淡な」。

en: An enclosed gear train.
That part of a car's transmission containing the train of gears, and to which the gear lever is connected.

ex.en: The car needs a new gearbox.
ex.ja: その車は変速機を交換する必要がある。

note.ja: gear（歯車）+ box（箱）。「変速機」。

en: An elemental (spirit or corporeal creature associated with a classical element) associated with earth.
One of a race of imaginary human-like beings, usually depicted as short and typically bearded males, who inhabit the inner parts of the e…

gnome.ety: From French gnome (“gnome”), from New Latin gnomus, used by Paracelsus as a synonym for pygmaeus (“pygmy”).

ex.en: There is a little garden gnome by the door.
ex.ja: ドアのそばに小さな庭の小人の置物がある。

note.ja: ラテン語 gnomus から。16世紀の錬金術師パラケルススの造語とされる。「地の精」。

ja: 銃口（at gunpoint：銃を突きつけられて）

en: A location in the front of the muzzle of a gun.
Threat or coercion by display or aiming a firearm or similar weapon.

ex.en: The bank clerk was held at gunpoint.
ex.ja: 銀行員は銃を突きつけられた。

note.ja: gun（銃）+ point（先端）。「銃口」。

en: Emotional distress or pain, often caused by a loved one or their absence.

heartache.ety: From Middle English heorteece, heorte-ece, from Old English heorteċe, equivalent to heart + ache. Blends both literal and figurative aspects, as emotional distress sometimes includes a physical element of chest discomfort. Compare heartbreak § Etymology, where the literal aspect is lesser, though it still can be said to have a physiological basis.

ex.en: I felt my heartaches, I was afraid of following you.
ex.ja: 心の痛みを感じたおまえを追うのが怖かった。

ex.en: His friend's cold shoulder caused him heartache.
ex.ja: 彼は友人の冷遇に心を痛めた。

note.ja: heart（心）+ ache（痛み）。「心痛」。headache と同じ作り。

en: Used to express approval, joy or victory.
goodbye.
A shout to signify victory.
An expression of excitement.
To shout an expression of excitement.

hooray.ety:
Unknown, first attested in the late 17th c. Possible etymologies:
* Alteration of huzzah. This is however questionable.
* From hurra in German, Danish, Swedish and Norwegian, húrra in Icelandic, hoera in Dutch.

ex.en: "Hooray! We won!"
ex.ja: 「万歳！勝ったぞ！」

note.ja: 歓声の擬声語。hurrah の変化形。「万歳」。

en: The characteristics that contribute to the differentiation or distinction of someone or something from a group of otherwise comparable id…
A person.

individuality.ety:
Etymology tree
English individual
Proto-Indo-European *-teh₂
Proto-Indo-European *-ts
Proto-Indo-European *-teh₂tsder.
Latin -itās
Old French -itebor.
Middle English -ite
English -ity
English individuality
From individual + -ity. Displaced native Old English hād.

ex.en: Individuality is very important in the West.
ex.ja: 西洋では個性は非常に重要である。

ex.en: He is a man of striking individuality.
ex.ja: あの人ははっきりした個性を持った人だ。

ex.en: Individuality is stressed in the Western world.
ex.ja: 西洋の世界では個性が強調される。

note.ja: individual（個人の）+ -ity。「個性」。

en: Twined or twisted together; entwined.
Inextricably related or relevant.

ex.en: Their lives are closely intertwined.
ex.ja: 彼らの人生は深く絡み合っている。

note.ja: intertwine（絡み合わせる）+ -ed。inter + twine（より糸）。two と同系。

en: Someone who looks after the maintenance and cleaning of a public building.
A caretaker or custodian; someone who maintains a school building specifically and may serve other administrative roles (the term caretak…

ex.en: The janitor cleans the school every evening.
ex.ja: 用務員は毎晩学校を掃除している。

note.ja: ラテン語 janitor（門番）から。janua（門）。January（門の神ヤヌスの月）と同じ。

en: Of or relating to judgment.
Inclined to rashly pass judgment, critical.

judgmental.ety:
Etymology tree
English judgment
Proto-Indo-European *h₂el-
Proto-Indo-European *-is

Old French -albor.

Old French -elbor.
▲

English judgmental
From judgment + -al.

ex.en: Try not to be judgmental about others.
ex.ja: 他人のことを決めつけないようにしなさい。

note.ja: judgment + -al。「批判的な・決めつける」。

en: A right to take possession of a debtor’s property as security until a debt or duty is discharged.

lien.ety: Borrowed from Middle French lien, from Latin ligāmen (“bond”), from ligō (“tie, bind”).

ex.en: The bank has a lien on the house.
ex.ja: 銀行はその家に担保権を持っている。

note.ja: フランス語 lien（ひも・きずな）から。ラテン語 ligamen。「担保権」。league と同じ lig。

en: An automobile body with seats and permanent top like a coupe, and with the top projecting over the driver and a projecting front.
An automobile with such a body.

limousine.ety: Borrowed from French limousine, from region Limousin, originally an adjective referring to the city Limoges, from Latin Lemovices (adjective Lemovicīnus), name of a Gaulish tribe in central France, most likely a reference to their elm bows and spears, of same ultimate origin as elm. First attested in 1902.

ex.en: Car? Ah, if you mean that limousine, - I chartered it.
ex.ja: 車？ああ・・・あのリムジンでしたら、私がチャーターした物ですわ。

note.ja: フランスのリムーザン地方（Limousin）の羊飼いのマントから。運転席を覆う屋根がそのマントに似ていたとされる。

en: Any of various deciduous trees of the genus Tilia, having heart-shaped leaves.
The soft wood of such trees.

linden.ety: From Middle English linden, from Old English linden (“linden”, adjective), from Proto-Germanic *lindīnaz, from Proto-Germanic *lindō (“linden tree”), equivalent to lind + -en. Cognate with Middle Low German linden (“linden”, adjective), German Low German Linnenboom (“linden-tree”), West Frisian linenbeam (“linden-tree”), German linden (“linden”, adjective). The English noun developed from the adjective.

ex.en: A linden tree stands in the town square.
ex.ja: 町の広場にシナノキが立っている。

note.ja: 古英語 lind（シナノキ）+ -en。「シナノキ・菩提樹」。

en: Of or relating to Lithuania.
The main language of Lithuania.
A person living in or coming from Lithuania.

Lithuanian.ety:
Etymology tree
English Lithuania
Proto-Indo-European *-nós
Proto-Italic *-nos
Proto-Italic *-ānos
Latin -ānus
Old French -ainder.
Middle English -an
English -an
English Lithuanian
From Lithuania + -an.

ex.en: Lithuanian is a good language.
ex.ja: リトアニア語はいい言語だ。

ex.en: I know a little tomcat that speaks Lithuanian.
ex.ja: 私はリトアニア語を話す小さなネコを知っています。

ex.en: Do you speak Lithuanian?
ex.ja: リトアニア語を話せますか？

note.ja: Lithuania + -an。「リトアニアの」。

en: A colourless, watery, coagulable bodily fluid which bathes the tissues and is carried by the lymphatic system into the bloodstream; it re…
The discharge from a sore, inflammation etc.

lymph.ety: Borrowing from French lymphe and/or Latin lympha (“clear water”), from Ancient Greek νῠ́μφη (nŭ́mphē, “bride; spring water”). Doublet of nymph.

ex.en: Lymph helps the body fight infection.
ex.ja: リンパ液は体が感染症と闘うのを助ける。

note.ja: ラテン語 lympha（清水）から。「リンパ液」。

en: To apply manure (as fertilizer or soil improver).
Animal excrement, especially that of common domestic farm animals and when used as fertilizer. Generally speaking, from cows, horses, she…
Any fertilizing substance, whether of animal origin or not; fertiliser.

manure.ety: From Middle English maynouren, manuren (“to supervise, toil”), borrowed from Anglo-Norman meinourer and Old French manovrer (whence also English maneuver, or in French manœuvrer) from Vulgar Latin *manuoperare (“work by hand”), from Latin manū (“by hand”) + operārī (“to work”). Displaced native (in the plural) Old English mes.

ex.en: Knowledge is like manure, it's only good when spread.
ex.ja: 知識というものは肥料と同じで、広まってこそ良いのである。

note.ja: ラテン語 manu operari（手で働く）から。手で耕して施すもの →「肥料（特に家畜のふん）」。

en: A ball of minced or ground meat, seasoned and cooked.
An easy pitch to hit, especially thrown right down the middle of the plate.

ex.en: Would you like to have some meatballs?
ex.ja: ミートボールはいかが？

ex.en: My grannie was crazy good at making meatballs.
ex.ja: うちのおばあちゃん、肉団子作るのすごく上手だったのよ。

ex.en: My grandma was really good at making meatballs.
ex.ja: うちのおばあちゃん、肉団子作るのすごく上手だったのよ。

note.ja: meat（肉）+ ball（球）。「ミートボール」。

en: Inflammation of the meninges, characterized by headache, neck stiffness and photophobia and also fever, chills, vomiting and myalgia.

meningitis.ety: From Ancient Greek μῆνῐγξ (mênĭnx) + -itis, equivalent to meninge + -itis.

ex.en: Meningitis is a serious infection.
ex.ja: 髄膜炎は深刻な感染症だ。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 mēninx（膜）+ -itis（炎症）。「髄膜炎」。

en: A metallic or stony object or body that is the remains of a meteoroid.

meteorite.ety:

From meteor + -ite.

ex.en: This hole was formed by a falling meteorite.
ex.ja: この穴はいん石の落下でできたものです。

note.ja: meteor（流星）+ -ite（石）。「隕石」。

en: Hatred of, contempt for, or prejudice against women.

misogyny.ety: From Ancient Greek μισογυνία (misogunía) and μισογύνης (misogúnēs, “woman hater”), from μισέω (miséō, “I hate”) + γυνή (gunḗ, “woman”). By surface analysis, miso- + -gyny.

ex.en: The book discusses misogyny in literature.
ex.ja: その本は文学における女性蔑視を論じている。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 misein（憎む）+ gynē（女性）。「女性嫌悪」。gynecology（婦人科）と同じ。

en: One who multiplies or causes something to increase.
A number by which another (the multiplicand) is to be multiplied.

ex.ja: 政府はその支出に乗数効果を期待している。

note.ja: multiply（掛ける）+ -er。「乗数」。

en: Not erect or perpendicular; not parallel to, or at right angles from, the base.
Not straightforward; indirect; by implication; (sometimes even) obscure, ambiguous, or confusing.
An oblique line.
Synonym of slash ⟨/⟩.
To deviate from a perpendicular line; to become askew.
To march in a direction oblique to the line of the column or platoon; — formerly accomplished by oblique steps, now by direct steps, the …

oblique.ety: From Middle French oblique, from Latin oblīquus (also spelled oblīcus) (“slanting, sideways, indirect, envious”).

ex.en: He made an oblique reference to the problem.
ex.ja: 彼はその問題に遠回しに触れた。

note.ja: ラテン語 obliquus（斜めの）から。「斜めの・遠回しの」。

en: Darkness; the absence of light.
The state of being unknown; a thing that is unknown.

obscurity.ety: From Middle English obscurite, obscuryte, from Middle French obscurité and its etymon Latin obscūritās. By surface analysis, obscure + -ity.

ex.en: He lived and died in obscurity.
ex.ja: 彼の一生は社会の下積みで終わった。

ex.en: He lived in obscurity.
ex.ja: 彼は埋もれ木の生活を送った。

note.ja: obscure（はっきりしない）+ -ity。「無名・不明瞭さ」。

en: A fierce attack.
A large number of people or things resembling an attack.

onslaught.ety: From on- + slaught. Formed after Middle Dutch aenslag, aenslach, equivalent to aen + slag, although slaught corresponds to Middle Dutch slacht; slag is cognate with the English weaving term sley. Compare Dutch aanslag and German Anschlag.

ex.en: The team faced an onslaught of attacks.
ex.ja: そのチームは猛攻撃にさらされた。

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 aanslag（攻撃）から。slaughter の影響を受けた。「猛攻撃」。

en: A mineral consisting, like quartz, of silica, but inferior to quartz in hardness and specific gravity, of the chemical formula SiO₂·nH₂O.
A precious gem, an iridescent gemstone found in the opal-silica mineral substrate (potch)

opal.ety:

Sanskrit उपल (upala)bor.

English opal
In Florio’s A World of Words 1598 as opale, from French opale, from Latin opalus, from Medieval Greek ὀπάλλιος (opállios), from Sanskrit उपल (upala, “gem, stone”), from उपरि (upári, “the upper millstone”). Distantly related to over.

ex.en: She wore an opal ring.
ex.ja: 彼女はオパールの指輪をしていた。

note.ja: サンスクリット語 upala（宝石）からギリシャ語・ラテン語を経た語。

en: Complete or partial muscle paralysis of a body part, often accompanied by a loss of feeling and uncontrolled body movements such as shaking.
To paralyse, either completely or partially.
Chummy, friendly.

palsy.ety: From Middle English palesie, from Anglo-Norman paralisie, parleisie et al., from Latin paralysis, from Ancient Greek παράλυσις (parálusis, “palsy”), from παραλύω (paralúō, “to disable on one side”), from παρα- (para-, “beside”) + λύω (lúō, “loosen”). Doublet of paralysis.

ex.en: He was born with cerebral palsy.
ex.ja: 彼は脳性まひを持って生まれた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 paralysis（麻痺）の短縮形。「麻痺」。

en: A group of civilians trained and organized in a military fashion, but which do not represent the formal forces of a sovereign power.
A member of a paramilitary group.
Relating to a paramilitary.

paramilitary.ety:
Etymology tree

Ancient Greek πᾰρᾰ- (pără-)der.

English military

From para- + military.

ex.en: A paramilitary group controlled the area.
ex.ja: 準軍事組織がその地域を支配していた。

note.ja: para（準ずる）+ military。「準軍事的な」。

en: Any bird of a number of genera in the family Phasianidae, notably in the genera Perdix and Alectoris.
The flesh or meat of this bird eaten as food.

partridge.ety: From Middle English partrich, partriche, pertriche, perdriz, from Old French perdriz, partriz, from Latin perdīx (“partridge”), from Ancient Greek πέρδιξ (pérdix, “partridge”), probably from πέρδομαι (pérdomai, “to fart”).

ex.en: A partridge flew out of the bushes.
ex.ja: ヤマウズラが茂みから飛び出した。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 perdix から古フランス語を経た語。「ヤマウズラ」。

en: permitted.
permissive
Any tool or device permitted for use in potentially explosive mine environments.

permissible.ety: From Middle English permyssyble, from Old French permissible, from Medieval Latin permissibilis.

ex.en: Is it permissible to take photos here?
ex.ja: ここで写真を撮っても構いませんか。

note.ja: permit + -ible。「許される」。

en: Neither sexual nor romantic in nature; being or exhibiting platonic love.

platonic.ety: Variant of Platonic, which see. The sense “non-sexual” dates to the 17th century in English, and to the 15th century in Latin; see platonic love for details.

ex.en: He's not my boyfriend, it's just platonic love with benefits!
ex.ja: 彼氏じゃないわ、利益をともなう純愛よ！

note.ja: プラトン（Plato）の。肉体的でない精神的な愛 →「プラトニックな」。

zh: 波爾卡音樂 /波尔卡音乐

en: A lively dance originating in Bohemia.
The music for this dance.
To dance the polka.

polka.ety: Via French and German from Czech polka, variant of půlka (“half”) as in "half-step"; see půl (“half”).

ex.en: Her dress is blue with white polka dots.
ex.ja: 彼女のドレスは青い地に白の水玉模様がある。

ex.en: Her skirt is yellow with polka dots.
ex.ja: 彼女のスカートは黄色で水玉模様がついている。

note.ja: チェコ語 půlka（半歩）とされる。またはポーランドの女性（Polka）から。

zh: 靈長目動物 /灵长目动物

en: A mammal of the order Primates, comprising of apes (including humans), monkeys, lemurs, tarsiers, lorisids, and galagos.
An anthropoid; ape including human.

primate.ety: First attested in 1876. From French primate, from the substantivization of Latin prīmās, prīmātis (“one of the first, chief, excellent, noble”), same as Etymology 2. So named due to the belief that primates are the highest order of mammals or animals.

ex.en: The primates include not only the apes, but also man.
ex.ja: 霊長類は尾の無いサルだけでなく人間も含む。

ex.en: Grooming in primates increases group cohesion.
ex.ja: 霊長類の毛づくろいは集団の結合を強める。

note.ja: ラテン語 primas（第一の地位の）から。prim（第一の）。動物界の最上位とされた →「霊長類」、教会の最高位 →「大主教」。

en: The act of capturing again.
That which is captured back; a prize retaken.
To capture something for a second or subsequent time, especially after a loss.
To capture an opponent's piece immediately after it has captured on the same square.

recapture.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Italic *wre-
Latin re-der.
Old French re-bor.
Middle English re-
English re-
English capture
English recapture
From re- + capture.

ex.en: The police hope to recapture the escaped prisoner soon.
ex.ja: 警察は逃げた囚人をすぐに再び捕まえたいと考えている。

note.ja: re（再び）+ capture（捕らえる）。「奪還する・再現する」。

en: Return or reversion to a certain state.
The instance of recurring; frequent occurrence.

recurrence.ety: From recurrent + -ence, cognate with Latin recurrentia, from recurrēns (“returning back, recurring”), form of recurrō (“to return, to recur”) (English recur).

ex.en: Is a recurrence likely?
ex.ja: 再発しますか。

ex.en: There's a slight possibility of a recurrence.
ex.ja: 再発の可能性が少しあります。

note.ja: re（再び）+ cur（走る）+ rence。再び起こること →「再発・繰り返し」。

en: The act, or the result of refining; the removal of impurities, or a purified material
High-class style; cultivation.

From refine + -ment.

ex.en: I read many books, and attained refinement.
ex.ja: 本をたくさん読んで、教養を付ける。

note.ja: refine（洗練する）+ -ment。「洗練・改良」。

en: A payment of time, effort or money to compensate for past transgression(s).

reparation.ety:
Etymology tree
Latin reparatus
Proto-Indo-European *-tis
Proto-Indo-European *-Hō

Proto-Italic *-tiō
Latin -tio
Latin reparātiō, reparātiōnisbor.
English reparation
Borrowed from Latin reparātiō, reparātiōnis.

ex.en: The country paid reparations after the war.
ex.ja: その国は戦後、賠償金を支払った。

note.ja: ラテン語 reparare（修理する）から。re（再び）+ par（整える）。元どおりに整えること →「賠償・償い」。repair と同じ。

en: To reject, put off (a request, demand etc.).
To ward off (a malignant influence, attack etc.).

repel.ety: From Middle English repellen, a borrowing from Old French *repeller, from Latin repellere (“to drive back”), from re- (“back”) + pellere (“to drive”). Doublet of repeal.

ex.en: There are plants that repel insects.
ex.ja: 昆虫を寄せつけない植物がある。

ex.en: The people could repel the invasion.
ex.ja: 人々は侵略を撃退することができた。

ex.en: He continues always being aggressive towards society, rather than repelling society and confining himself.
ex.ja: 彼は社会を忌避して自分の中に閉じこもるというよりは、社会に対して常に攻撃的な態度をとり続けた。

note.ja: re（後ろへ）+ pel（押す）。押し返す →「撃退する・はじく・不快にさせる」。

en: To improve, renew, renovate, or revise (something).
An act of improving, renewing, renovating, or revising something; an improvement, renovation, revamping, or revision.

revamp.ety: The verb is derived from re- (prefix meaning ‘again, anew’) + vamp (“to patch, repair, or refurbish”). The noun is derived from the verb.

ex.en: The restaurant revamped its menu.
ex.ja: そのレストランはメニューを一新した。

note.ja: re（再び）+ vamp（靴の甲を張り替える）。「改良する・刷新する」。

A control surface on the vertical stabilizer of a fixed-wing aircraft or an autogyro. On some craft, the entire vertical stabilizer compr…

See also Dutch and West Frisian roer, German Ruder; also akin to Old English rōwan (“to row”). More at rōwan, -þor.

ex.en: The captain turned the rudder.
ex.ja: 船長はかじを切った。

note.ja: 古英語 rōther（櫂）から。row（漕ぐ）と同系。「かじ」。

en: Synonym of sailor, particularly on a maritime vessel.
A person of the lowest rank in the Navy, below able seaman.

seaman.ety: From Middle English seeman, seman, from Old English sǣmann. Cognate with Saterland Frisian Seemon (“seaman, sailor”), West Frisian seeman (“seaman, sailor”), Dutch zeeman (“seaman, sailor”), German Low German Seemann (“seaman, sailor”), German Seemann (“seaman, sailor”), Swedish sjöman (“seaman, sailor”), Norwegian sjømann (“seaman, sailor”). Equivalent to sea + -man.

ex.en: The young seaman was on his first voyage.
ex.ja: その若い船員にとっては初めての航海だった。

note.ja: sea（海）+ man。「船員・水兵」。

en: Emotions or feelings arising from or relating to aesthetic or moral standards, especially those which are sensitive and thus likely to be…
The ability to feel, perceive, or sense; responsiveness to sensory stimuli; sensitivity; also, the degree to which someone or something (…

sensibility.ety: From Late Middle English sensibilite (“physical ability to sense or perceive; sensitivity to pain; type of perception by a sense organ; perception, understanding; image imprinted on the mind during perception; (philosophy) capacity of the soul to receive information from the senses, perceptibility; (in the plural) the senses”), from Middle French sensibilité and Old French sensibilité (“characteristic or state of being capable of sensation”) (modern French sensibilité), and from their etymon Late Latin sēnsibilitās (“intelligence; perception, sensation; sensitiveness; meaning or sense of words

ex.en: I can't compete with the delicate sensibility of Tom.
ex.ja: トムの繊細な感受性にはかなわない。

note.ja: sens（感じる）+ ibility。感じ取る力 →「感受性・感性」。

en: A very tall building with a large number of floors.
Anything very tall or high.

skyscraper.ety: Compound of sky + scraper, first applied to tall steel-frame buildings in American cities such as New York City and Chicago in the 1880s.

ex.en: The skyscraper rose above the other buildings around.
ex.ja: その摩天楼はまわりの他の建物の上方にそびえていた。

ex.en: The buildings are small in comparison with the skyscrapers in New York.
ex.ja: そのビルはニューヨークの摩天楼と比べると小さい。

ex.en: They demolished the old temple to build a skyscraper.
ex.ja: 高層ビルを建てるために、そのお寺は取り壊された。

note.ja: sky（空）+ scraper（こするもの）。「空をこするほど高い建物」→「超高層ビル」。

en: A very light state of sleep, almost awake.
A very heavy state of sleep.
To be in a very light state of sleep, almost awake.
To be inactive or negligent.

slumber.ety:
From Middle English slombren, slomren, frequentative of Middle English slummen, slumen (“to doze”), probably from Middle English slume (“slumber”), from Old English slūma, from Proto-Germanic *slūm- (“slack, loose, limp, flabby”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)lew- (“loose, limp, flabby”).
Cognate with West Frisian slommerje, slûmerje (“to slumber”), Dutch sluimeren (“to slumber”), German schlummern (“to slumber, doze”), Swedish slummer (“to slumber”). By surface analysis, sloom + -er.

ex.en: Mary and Alice are having a slumber party.
ex.ja: メアリーとアリスはお泊まり会をしています。

ex.en: He fell into a slumber inadvertently.
ex.ja: 彼はついうとうととした。

ex.en: She woke from her slumber.
ex.ja: 彼女は目ざめた。

note.ja: 中英語 slumeren から。擬音的な語。「眠り」。

en: Not permitting water or some other liquid to escape or penetrate; watertight.
Impermeable to air or other gases; airtight.
Synonym of afterdamp (“suffocating gases present in a coal mine after an explosion caused by firedamp”).

staunch.ety:
From Middle English staunch, staunche (“(adjective) in good condition or repair; solidly made, firm; watertight; of a person or wound: not bleeding; certain; intact; (adverb) firmly, soundly”) [and other forms], from Anglo-Norman estaunche, Old French estanche (“firm; watertight”) (modern French étanche (“airtight; watertight”)), a variant of estanc (“a pond”), from estanchier (“to stop the flow of a liquid (blood, water, etc.); to make (something) watertight; to quench (thirst)”) (modern French étancher), possibly from one of the following:
* From Vulgar Latin *stagnicāre, from Latin stāgnum

ex.en: She is a staunch supporter of the team.
ex.ja: 彼女はそのチームの熱心な支持者だ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 estanche（水漏れしない）から。「しっかりした」→「忠実な・断固とした」。

en: Rigidity or a measure of rigidity.
Inflexibility or a measure of inflexibility.

stiffness.ety: From Middle English stiffenes, styffenesse, styfnesse; equivalent to stiff + -ness. Perhaps merging with Middle English stithnesse, stithnysse, from Old English stīþness (“stiffness”).

ex.en: I felt some stiffness in my neck.
ex.ja: 首に少しこわばりを感じた。

note.ja: stiff（硬い）+ -ness。「こわばり」。

en: Having attained synchronization, together, coordinated, combined.

ex.en: The 'gold' yearned for by the Japanese synchronized swimming world was not quite reached.
ex.ja: 日本シンクロ界の悲願である金には、あと一歩で届かなかった。

note.ja: synchronize + -ed。ギリシャ語 syn（共に）+ khronos（時）。「同期した」→ synchronized swimming。sync と同じ。

en: Television.
A television set.
Inclined to telling (by explicitly stating facts), instead of showing (by conveying an impression so that events are described in the nar…

ex.en: "Did you watch telly last week?" "No."
ex.ja: 「あなたは先週テレビを見ましたか」「いいえ」

ex.en: I haven't got a telly at home.
ex.ja: 家にテレビ、ないんだ。

ex.en: We watch telly all the time.
ex.ja: テレビばっかり見てます。

note.ja: television の短縮。（英口語）「テレビ」。

en: An elongated, boneless, flexible organ or limb of some animals, such as the octopus and squid.
One of the glandular hairs on the leaves of certain insectivorous plants.
To move like a tentacle

tentacle.ety: From New Latin tentāculum, from tentō. Doublet of tentaculum.

ex.en: An octopus has eight tentacles.
ex.ja: タコには８本の触手がある。

note.ja: ラテン語 tentaculum から。tentare（触れる・試す）。「触手」。tempt と同じ。

en: The branch of mathematics dealing with those properties of a geometrical object (of arbitrary dimensionality) that are unchanged by conti…
Any collection τ of subsets of a given set X that contains both the empty set and X, and which is closed under finitary intersections and…

topology.ety: From Late Latin topologia, from By surface analysis, topo- (“place”) + -logy (“study of, a branch of knowledge”).

ex.en: The network topology shows how computers are connected.
ex.ja: ネットワークの構成図はコンピューターがどうつながっているかを示している。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 topos（場所）+ logia（学）。「位相幾何学・構成」。topic と同じ。

en: Beyond, spanning or crossing, or on or from the other side of the Atlantic Ocean.

transatlantic.ety:

Proto-Italic *trāns
Proto-Italic *trāns-
Latin trans-bor.
English trans-

From trans- + Atlantic.

ex.en: Lindbergh's solo nonstop transatlantic flight was a remarkable accomplishment.
ex.ja: リンドバーグの大西洋横断無着陸単独飛行はめざましい偉業であった。

note.ja: trans（越えて）+ Atlantic（大西洋）。「大西洋横断の」。

en: Not controlled; not under control.
Lacking the usual traffic control devices, such as traffic lights, pedestrian signals, pavement markings, traffic signs, or a crossing gu…

uncontrolled.ety:

Proto-Indo-European *n̥-
Proto-Germanic *un-
Proto-West Germanic *un-
Old English un-
Middle English un-
English un-
English controlled
English uncontrolled
From un- + controlled.

ex.en: Americans appear unsettled and uncontrolled to Japanese.
ex.ja: 日本人からが、アメリカ人は不安定で、自由奔放に見える。

note.ja: un + controlled。「制御されない」。

en: Open and not yet settled or determined.
Uncommitted, not having reached a decision.
A voter etc. who has not yet come to a decision.

undecided.ety: From Middle English undecided, equivalent to un- + decided.

ex.en: It is still undecided when we will begin.
ex.ja: いつ始めるのかはまだ決まっていない。

ex.en: I'm still undecided whether to go by car or by train.
ex.ja: 車で行くか電車で行くかまだ迷ってる。

ex.en: The lawsuit remains undecided.
ex.ja: 訴訟は未決である。

note.ja: un（否定）+ decided（決まった）。「未決定の」。

en: Having no parallel; without equal; lacking anything similar or worthy of comparison.

unparalleled.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *né
Proto-Indo-European *n̥-
Proto-Germanic *un-
Proto-West Germanic *un-
Old English un-
Middle English un-
English un-
English paralleled
English unparalleled
From un- + paralleled.

ex.en: The view from the tower is unparalleled.
ex.ja: 塔からの眺めは比類がない。

note.ja: un + paralleled（匹敵された）。「並ぶものがない」→「比類のない」。parallel と同じ。

en: Not requested; neither welcomed nor invited.

unsolicited.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *né
Proto-Indo-European *n̥-
Proto-Germanic *un-
Proto-West Germanic *un-
Old English un-
Middle English un-
English un-
English solicited
English unsolicited
From un- + solicited.

ex.en: I keep getting unsolicited emails.
ex.ja: 頼んでもいないメールが次々に届く。

note.ja: un + solicited（求められた）。「頼まれていない・一方的な」。solicit と同じ。

en: To remove a veil from; to uncover; to reveal something hidden.
To show, especially for the first time.

unveil.ety:
From Middle English *unveilen (suggested by past participle unveiled, vnueylyd (“unveiled”)). Equivalent to un- + veil. Ultimately from Latin velum (whence also English voile, English reveal, Russian вуа́ль (vuálʹ), Russian завуали́ровать (zavualírovatʹ) (compare typologically)).
Also compare typologically uncloak, unmask, Russian разобла́чать (razobláčatʹ) (akin to облаче́ние (oblačénije)).

ex.en: He is not eager to unveil his main argument.
ex.ja: 彼は主たる論点を明らかにすることに気乗り薄である。

note.ja: un（取り去る）+ veil（ベール）。「ベールを取る」→「公開する」。

en: Not worthy; lacking value or merit; worthless.
An inadequate person.

unworthy.ety: From Middle English unworthy, equivalent to un- + worthy.

ex.en: Such conduct is unworthy of a teacher.
ex.ja: 教師にあるまじき行為だ。

ex.en: They are unworthy of the praise given them.
ex.ja: 彼らは与えられた賞賛に値しない。

note.ja: un + worthy。「値しない」。
